Troubleshooting · BEGINNER FRIENDLY · 6 MIN READ

Wi-Fi connected. Internet missing?

Tech Compass · Updated 2026-10-19

IN THIS GUIDE

The quick answer1. Check the basics2. Try another device3. Reconnect and restart4. Check device settings5. Get specific helpFurther reading
THE QUICK ANSWER

First check whether the problem affects one device or every device. That tells you whether to start with your computer or your network. Try the steps below in order and test after each one.

1. Check the basics

Make sure Wi-Fi is on and airplane mode is off. Confirm you joined your own network. Open a second website: if only one site fails, your connection may be working.

2. Try another device

Connect a phone to the same Wi-Fi and temporarily turn off mobile data. If it also cannot get online, check your provider’s outage page using mobile data. If only your computer fails, concentrate on that computer.

3. Reconnect and restart

Turn Wi-Fi off and back on. Save your work and restart the affected device. If multiple devices fail, restart the router using its power switch or manufacturer instructions. This temporarily disconnects everyone; do not press the factory-reset button.

4. Check device settings

On Windows, use Settings → Network & internet and the network troubleshooter in Get Help. On a Mac, check System Settings → Wi-Fi and the network recommendations if shown. Move closer to the router to test whether distance or interference is involved.

5. Get specific help

If the problem continues, record the error message, affected devices, and whether the network appears. Contact your internet provider for a whole-network failure or your device support team for a device-only failure. Avoid a network reset until you understand which saved network and VPN settings it removes.
